findings.title: Propagate compound patch validation to renderer stream handlers
findings.description: The new getByPath/setByPath rejection outcomes are not handled by the older renderer applyPatch implementations. Built React useUIStream processing move from /state/source to /state/items/01 removes source then silently rejects its destination. Copy/move from /state/items/01 to a valid key creates an own undefined property. Core applySpecStreamPatch safely rejects the same compound patches, but these handlers bypass it. This introduces data loss when noncanonical input previously coerced to index 1.
findings.scope_notes: Direct runtime evidence is React. Solid, Vue, Svelte and React Native have corresponding read-remove-write code by static inspection; do not claim those framework runtimes were exercised.
findings.recommendation: Route all public streaming patch handlers through the safe compound helper, or validate source and post-removal destination before mutating.

findings.title: Exclude rejected batch entries from state-provider change callbacks
findings.description: After update({"/items/01":"rejected","/count":1}), new core state correctly preserves items but StateProvider onStateChange reports both entries because it compares submitted values with the old snapshot. Applications persisting callbacks receive a write that never occurred. Exact base executed the coerced array write, so the same callback matched its state; the new rejection exposes this mismatch.
findings.scope_notes: Direct built React StateProvider and DOM evidence. Svelte/Vue/Solid callback builders use the same old-snapshot comparison by static inspection.
findings.recommendation: Derive emitted change records from accepted writes and the committed state, preserving append and sequential batch semantics.

issue_candidates.title: Overlapping valid update callbacks can omit a later restoration
issue_candidates.description: With user.name=a, update({"/user":{name:"b"},"/user/name":"a"}) ends with a but callback contains only parent b on both exact base and head. Earlier introduced attribution was refuted and sent to coordinator.
